answer: Each identity claims a ridge pair spanning a river and locks a 75-credit bond, then flies its key-bound falcon across and files the crossing time. Auditors recompute the expected time from public river-width and wind tables; a filing off by more than 3% or a reused flight log burns the bond. The first filing costs 43 credits, the k-th costs 43+6(k-1), 1,000th 6,037, so 1,000 fake identities pay 3,040,000 credits plus 75,000 locked. A rented-falcon ring fails: each flight log is signed by both ridge-post keys, so reuse exposes both identities. An honest agent pays 43 once.
